source.citation: Chen et al. (2022), Computers, Environment and Urban Systems 92, 101749
source.coefficient_precision: rounded as printed in Figure 2 of the paper

feature.name: TNTL
feature.semantic_definition: sum of valid annual nighttime-light pixel intensities within one city boundary
feature.ntl_product: EOG/Colorado School of Mines SNPP-VIIRS Version 1 monthly vcm composites
feature.paper_temporal_composite: pixelwise annual median of monthly images
paper_preprocessing_summary: use Beijing and Shanghai city-centre maxima as reference caps for abnormal high values
replace values above the cap elsewhere with the maximum of the eight neighbouring pixels
use the product's zeroed stray-light-contaminated high-latitude summer pixels

selection_evidence.paper_basis: lowest reported RMSE and a saturating relationship consistent with the high-DEI plateau; the quadratic form had a slightly higher R2

limitations: No legacy serialized model was recovered.
No matched city-year DEI, TNTL, and boundary training table was available for retraining.
The paper does not report MAE, cross-validation, holdout validation, residuals, or full-precision coefficients.
The paper does not identify the exact city-boundary source or version, projection, pixel-area weighting, or missing-month policy.
The printed coefficients are rounded and therefore cannot reproduce an unavailable full-precision fitted model exactly.
ANTL is not interchangeable with TNTL.
Predictions for years outside 2017-2020 are unsupported.
